review_status: Draft for clinical and patient review
title: Pembrolizumab + pemetrexed + carboplatin (AUC 5)
purpose: This combination treats a type of lung cancer called metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. Your team checks the cancer's features, your health and your priorities before recommending it. Ask what benefit is realistic for you and how it will be measured.

agents.name: Pembrolizumab
agents.explanation: Cancer can use a stop signal to quieten immune cells. Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1, helping those cells stay active against cancer. It does not work for everyone.
agents.watch: The immune system can also inflame healthy organs. New cough, diarrhoea, unusual weakness, severe headache, thirst or a spreading rash need prompt advice. Effects can start during treatment or after it finishes.

agents.name: Pemetrexed
agents.explanation: Cells need chemical building blocks to copy their DNA. Pemetrexed blocks enzymes involved in making those building blocks, slowing cancer-cell growth.
agents.watch: Healthy tissues can be affected too: low blood counts, a sore mouth, rash and kidney problems are important. Folic acid, vitamin B12 and prescribed steroids help reduce particular risks.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin binds to DNA and damages it, making it harder for a cancer cell to copy or repair its instructions. AUC 5 is a dosing target; your team calculates the dose using kidney function.
agents.watch: Low blood counts, nausea and vomiting can occur. An allergic reaction is also possible: tell the nurse immediately if you feel flushed, itchy, tight-chested or unwell during the drip.

phases.label: Induction · cycles 1–4
phases.detail: All three medicines on Day 1, once every 21 days, for up to four cycles. Your team may adjust the plan.

phases.label: Maintenance · after induction
phases.detail: Carboplatin stops. Pembrolizumab and pemetrexed may continue every 21 days while appropriate. Duration and changes are agreed with your oncology team.

timeline.label: Blood counts / infection
timeline.text: Counts may fall between visits · timing varies

timeline.label: Immune effects
timeline.text: Any day · also after treatment ends

day_groups.title: Your infusion day
day_groups.body: Your team checks symptoms and blood results before treatment. Tell your nurse immediately about pain at the drip site, itching, flushing or breathing changes. The time in hospital includes checks and preparation, not just infusion time.
day_groups.action: Before leaving, check your take-home medicines, contact details and next appointment.

day_groups.title: The first days at home
day_groups.body: Feeling sick can start on treatment day or later. Appetite, taste, sleep or bowel habits may change. Take prescribed supportive medicines as directed; ask for help if they are not controlling symptoms.
day_groups.action: Contact the team if vomiting persists, you cannot keep fluids down, or you develop new diarrhoea. Do not assume diarrhoea is ordinary chemotherapy upset.

day_groups.title: Keep checking how you feel
day_groups.body: Blood counts may be reduced between treatments. You cannot tell your count from the date or from how well you feel. Fatigue or mouth symptoms may affect eating and daily activity.
day_groups.action: Use the urgent advice below for fever, shivering or suddenly feeling unwell, including with a normal temperature.

day_groups.title: Prepare for your next review
day_groups.body: Some symptoms may settle; others can continue or appear for the first time. Improvement does not prove your blood counts have recovered. The next treatment depends on your review and tests.
day_groups.action: Bring your symptom record and questions. Confirm the next appointment: the next Day 1 is usually 21 days after this cycle's Day 1, if treatment proceeds.

support.title: Folic acid + vitamin B12
support.text: These reduce pemetrexed toxicity. Take folic acid as prescribed; the team arranges B12 injections. If you missed preparation, tell the team before treatment.

support.title: Steroids + anti-sickness medicines
support.text: Follow your own written schedule. Steroids can help prevent pemetrexed rash; anti-sickness medicines prevent or treat nausea. Check which are regular and which are only when needed.

support.title: Medicines check
support.text: Bring your complete medicines list. Ask before adding painkillers, supplements or herbal products. A stomach-protection medicine may be included in your prescription; do not omit prescribed medicines based on this page.

support.title: Tests + symptom review
support.text: Blood counts and organ-function tests help the team assess safety. Tell them about symptoms even if the blood results look reassuring. Scans assess cancer response according to your plan.

questions.q: How will we know if it is helping?
questions.a: Ask your oncologist what the treatment is aiming to achieve for you, when scans are planned and what would lead to continuing, changing or stopping it. How you feel and the amount of side effects do not reliably show how well treatment is working.

questions.q: Why might a cycle be delayed?
questions.a: A delay can give time to recover or investigate a new symptom. It is a safety decision, not a personal failure. Ask which medicines are affected, what needs to improve and when you will be reviewed.

questions.q: Will I get every side effect?
questions.a: No. The body map shows selected possibilities, not a prediction. Ask about common effects, serious less common effects, and any long-term risks that matter particularly to you. The same symptom can have several causes.

questions.q: What should I organise before starting?
questions.a: Confirm blood-test and Day Ward arrangements, transport home, your medicines schedule and a thermometer. Keep the oncology contact instructions and immunotherapy alert card available. Ask for an interpreter or accessible information if useful.

questions.q: What else belongs in the consent conversation?
questions.a: Your priorities, expected benefit, alternatives including supportive care, fertility, contraception, pregnancy or breastfeeding, work, driving and the possibility of lasting side effects. You can ask more questions or reconsider treatment at any stage.
